summary: Michael Hookham works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Chögyam Trungpa (1965) and Dilgo Khyentse, and he founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He earned a BA (ca. 1976–1980) and a doctorate (ca. 1980–1984) at the University of London. At SOAS, he served as a fellow, department head, and Associate Dean.

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town (B.Soc.Sc., ca. 1986–1989) and the University of California, Santa Barbara (M.A., ca. 1991–1994), completing doctoral work under William F. Powell.

Michael Janda is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna (PhD, 1988–1996) and habilitated at the University of Zurich. He held an assistant post at Zurich (1995) and a chair at the University of Münster (2002).

Michael Jansen was an archaeologist and historian educated at Bonn, Sapienza, Delhi, the Archaeological Survey of India, and RWTH Aachen (PhD ca. 1974–1979). He served as dean at RWTH Aachen, founding rector at GUtech Oman, and president of the Research Centre Indian Ocean.

Michael Jay Sweet worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, studying under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Richard Hugh Robinson, and traditional teachers, and later served as a clinical assistant professor of psychiatry there.

Michael Jerryson was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his undergraduate education at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (ca. 1994–1998). He taught religious studies at Eckerd College (ca. 2008–2012) and Youngstown State University (ca. 2012–2021).

Michael Kowalewski is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies at the University of Cambridge from 1969 to 1972 and at SOAS University of London from 1987 to 1990.

Michael L. Walter was a scholar of Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied under Larry William Moses. He held posts as a research fellow at the Lumbini International Research Institute and as a special languages cataloger at Indiana University.
Michael M. Broido is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Cambridge from ca. 1963 to 1967 and later held a post at the University of Oxford.

Michael Oppitz is a Tibetologist and anthropologist. He held a position at the Institute for Advanced Study, Berlin (ca. 1987–1988) and served as director at the University of Zurich from ca. 1990 to 2008.
Michael P. Berman works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has served as a professor at Brock University and as managing editor of the Canadian Journal of Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2012.

Michael Puett is a historian, sinologist, and philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago (ca. 1987–1994) studying under Marshall Sahlins and Anthony C. Yu. In ca. 1994, he joined the faculty at Harvard University.

Michael Pye is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. Educated at Cambridge and the University of Leeds (Ph.D., ca. 1972–1976), he held academic posts at Leeds, Lancaster, and as professor of religious studies at the University of Marburg.

Michael R. Sheehy specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2007) under Steven D. Goodman and held posts at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center and the University of Virginia.

Michael Radich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Harvard (ca. 2001–2007). He held posts at Victoria University of Wellington (2005–2017) and became Professor of Buddhist Studies at Heidelberg University in 2018.

Michael Rostovtzeff was a historian and archaeologist who studied in Kyiv and St. Petersburg University. He held academic posts at St. Petersburg, the Bestuzhev Courses, the University of Oxford (1918–1920), the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1920–1925), and Yale University (1925–1939).
Michael S. Drummond is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol and was a PhD candidate at Utrecht University (attested 2006).

Michael Schmidt is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts with the Katalogisierung der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1992) and at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a dictionary editor and contributor.
Michael Silverstein was a linguist who studied at Stuyvesant High School and Harvard University (ca. 1962–1971). He held an academic post at the University of Chicago from ca. 1970 to 2020.
